# Deploy RisingWave Streaming Database on Railway

Kafka, Postgres CDC, materialized views: real-time Apache Flink alternative

[![Deploy on Railway](https://railway.com/button.svg)](https://railway.com/deploy/risingwave-streaming-database)

## About

![RisingWave](https://github.com/risingwavelabs.png)

RisingWave is an open source streaming database. You write PostgreSQL-compatible SQL, and it keeps
materialized views continuously up to date as data arrives from Kafka, Postgres CDC, MySQL CDC,
webhooks and ten more sources. Any Postgres client, driver or BI tool connects to it.
It does in one system what a Debezium plus Kafka plus Flink plus serving-database stack does in
four, and you query the results with a plain SELECT.

Official intro video (click to watch on YouTube):

[![Watch: What is RisingWave?](https://img.youtube.com/vi/98sahakm6I4/hqdefault.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=98sahakm6I4)

This template runs the official RisingWave image in single-node mode: one process carrying the SQL
frontend, compute, metadata and compaction, reachable over the Postgres wire protocol by any
Postgres client, driver or BI tool. The password for the `root`, `postgres` and `rwadmin` users is
generated for your deployment and applied on every deployment, so you copy `DATABASE_PUBLIC_URL`
and connect with no setup step. Memory is set to the 8 GiB RisingWave expects; you can raise it for
heavier workloads, but do not lower it below 8 GiB because that can cause issues like a crash-loop.

RisingWave's web dashboard can be accessed at your service URL, behind its own login. Normally it is not
safe to expose the dashboard: it has no built-in authentication. This template fixes that by
putting an authenticating proxy in front of it, with a second generated password, so you get the
dashboard without compromising on safety.

## What gets deployed

| Service | Source | Type |
|---------|--------|------|
| RisingWave | `risingwavelabs/risingwave:v3.0.3` | TCP service |

## Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Description |
| --------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `PORT` | 8080 | [Do not change] Port of the dashboard's authenticating proxy. Railway's public domain and healthcheck both point here. |
| `RW_PASSWORD` | (secret) | Password for the root, postgres and rwadmin database users, auto-generated and applied automatically on every deployment (To change passwords, change this value and redeploy). |
| `DATABASE_URL` | - | [Do not change] Connection string for other services in this project, over the private network. |
| `RW_LISTEN_ADDR` | [::]:4566 | [Do not change] SQL port bind. |
| `RW_PARALLELISM` | 4 | How many parallel actors each streaming job runs. 4 suits small and medium workloads; |
| `ENABLE_TELEMETRY` | false | Set to true to share anonymous usage statistics with RisingWave Labs. |
| `RW_DASHBOARD_USER` | (secret) | Username for the web dashboard login. Clearing it falls back to root. |
| `DATABASE_PUBLIC_URL` | - | [Do not change] Connection string from outside Railway (psql, BI tools etc). Credentials are included. |
| `RW_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` | (secret) | Password for the web dashboard at your public URL. Different from the database password; Changing it takes effect on the next redeploy. |
| `RW_TOTAL_MEMORY_BYTES` | 8589934592 | Memory budget in bytes (default 8 GiB, the documented minimum). |
| `RW_SINGLE_NODE_STORE_DIRECTORY` | /var/lib/risingwave | [Do not change] Where data gets stored on the Volume. |
| `RW_SECRET_STORE_PRIVATE_KEY_HEX` | (secret) | Encrypts credentials you store with CREATE SECRET. |

## Configuration

- **Start command:** `sh -c 'printf "%s" "frontend.hba_config.entries = [{ connection_type = \"Host\", databases = [\"all\"], users = [\"all\"], addresses = [\"all\"], auth_method = \"password\" }]" > /tmp/risingwave.toml && echo "" | base64 -d > /tmp/Bootstrap.java && echo "" | base64 -d > /tmp/dashproxy.py && (java -cp "/risingwave/bin/connector-node/libs/*" /tmp/Bootstrap.java &) ; (python3 /tmp/dashproxy.py &) ; exec /risingwave/bin/risingwave single_node --config-path /tmp/risingwave.toml --total-memory-bytes "$RW_TOTAL_MEMORY_BYTES" --parallelism "$RW_PARALLELISM"'`
- **Healthcheck:** `/api/version`
- **Networking:** Public domain with automatic HTTPS
- **TCP Proxies:** 4566
- **Volume:** `/var/lib/risingwave`

**Category:** Storage

[View on Railway →](https://railway.com/deploy/risingwave-streaming-database)
